finding_key: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/data-validation.ts::`value.touppercase()` is now called on a value that was only ever compared with `===` before — any non-string `cell.v` reaching the render path throws instead of rendering unchecked

verdict.reasoning: The new branch in `data-validation.ts` (`return value.toUpperCase() === CHECKBOX_TRUE;`) would indeed throw on a non-string, but the claim never establishes that a non-string `Cell.v` can arrive: `Cell` declares `v?: string` in `model/core/types.ts`, and the caller `renderCellCheckbox` in `view/gridcanvas.ts` passes `cell?.v` under that type. The same file already calls string methods on the identically-typed parameter — `isValidListValue` uses `value?.trim()` and `isValidDateValue` uses `value.trim()` — and `renderCellContent` does `data.split('\n')` on `cell?.v`, so a non-string `v` would already break the list/date/text render paths; the change adds no new fragility class. The claim even admits it is unconfirmed ("one would need a store/import path that can persist a non-string `v`"), so as written it is a speculative hardening suggestion, not a defect present in the code; I mark confidence medium only because I could not inspect the xlsx/Yorkie/REST ingestion paths myself.
